html:
An Islamic reform movement founded in Yogyakarta in 1912 by the preacher Ahmad Dahlan. It is one of the two largest Muslim organisations in Indonesia.

Dahlan had studied in Mecca and read the Egyptian reformer Muhammad Abduh. He wanted Muslims to return to the Quran and the example of the Prophet, set aside local customs mixed into worship, and think for themselves about Islamic law rather than simply follow old scholars.

He also believed Muslims in the Dutch East Indies fell behind because they lacked modern schooling. So Muhammadiyah built schools that taught science and Dutch alongside religion, then hospitals, clinics, orphanages and later universities. Its women's wing, Aisyiyah, founded in 1917, ran girls' schools.

It became a model of modern Islam that works through social service rather than politics. The traditionalist Nahdlatul Ulama, founded in 1926, rose partly in answer to it. Today Muhammadiyah runs thousands of schools and claims tens of millions of followers.
sum: An Islamic reform movement founded in Yogyakarta in 1912 by the preacher Ahmad Dahlan. It is one of the two largest Muslim organisations in Indonesia.
